overview: Niger is a large landlocked country in West Africa, named after the Niger river. Its capital and largest city is Niamey. Niger became independent from France in 1960. It has one of the fastest-growing populations in the world and large deposits of uranium.

geography.text: More than three-quarters of Niger is in the Sahara Desert, including the Aïr Mountains and the Ténéré desert. The south is the dry Sahel, where most people live and farm, and the Niger river flows through the south-west, past Niamey.

history.text: Parts of Niger belonged to the Songhai Empire and the Hausa city-states, and Agadez was a key stop on trans-Saharan trade routes. France colonised Niger in the early 1900s, and it became independent in 1960. It is a major producer of uranium. The military seized power in 2023.

events.title: Agadez
events.text: Agadez becomes a major desert trading town.

events.title: Coup
events.text: The army overthrows the elected president.

government.text: Niger has been ruled by the military since July 2023, when soldiers overthrew the elected President, Mohamed Bazoum. The junta expelled French troops and, with Mali and Burkina Faso, left ECOWAS to form the Alliance of Sahel States.

economy.text: Niger is one of the poorest countries in the world. It is a major producer of uranium and has begun exporting oil through a pipeline to Benin. Most people are farmers and herders.

culture.text: Most of Niger is in the Sahara and Sahel. Agadez's mud-brick minaret, one of the tallest in the world, is a UNESCO site. The Gerewol festival of the Wodaabe people, where young men dance to impress women, is famous.

items.title: Gerewol
items.text: A Wodaabe festival of dance and beauty.

sport.text: Football and traditional wrestling are the most popular sports; the national wrestling championship is a big event. Abdoul Razak Issoufou won taekwondo silver at the 2016 Olympics.

items.title: Traditional wrestling
items.text: The national sport, with a yearly championship.

didYouKnow: Niger is home to West Africa's last wild giraffes.
Dinosaur fossils, including Nigersaurus, have been found in Niger's desert.
